attractions.name: Nanga Parbat Viewpoint (Fairy Meadows)
attractions.description: A stunning alpine meadow offering close-up views of Nanga Parbat, the world's ninth-highest peak, reached by jeep and a short trek.

attractions.name: Chilas Rock Carvings
attractions.description: Thousands of ancient Buddhist-era petroglyphs and inscriptions carved into rocks along the old Silk Road route, dating back over a thousand years.

travel_tips.tip: Visit Diamer between May and October — many higher areas are snowed in or inaccessible in winter.
A 4x4 jeep is often necessary for side valleys and glacier viewpoints; book local drivers in advance during peak season (July-August).
Roads can be affected by landslides, especially after rain — check current road conditions before travel, particularly along the Karakoram Highway.

history.founded: A historic district headquartered at Chilas, along the ancient route now followed by the Karakoram Highway
history.city_history: Diamer District is home to Nanga Parbat, the world's ninth-highest peak and one of the most dangerous mountains to climb, historically nicknamed the 'Killer Mountain'. Chilas has been a trade and travel waypoint on the Silk Road for centuries.
history.province_history: Gilgit-Baltistan is a mountainous region in northern Pakistan, home to some of the world's highest peaks including K2, Nanga Parbat, and parts of the Karakoram, Himalaya, and Hindu Kush ranges. Historically composed of small princely states (including Hunza and Nagar) along the ancient Silk Road, the region acceded to Pakistan in 1947-48 and is administered separately from Azad Kashmir, with its own Legislative Assembly since 2009.
